title: The thirsty crow.
lines: It was a hot, hot summer's day.
The sun was blazing.
The grass was yellow and dry.
The flowers drooped.
And all the streams and puddles had dried up.
High in the sky flew a black crow.
He had been flying all day, and he was so thirsty.
Caw, caw, he said in a croaky voice.
Water, I need water.
He flew over the fields.
No water.
He flew over the village.
No water.
He got tired and his wings got heavy.
And then he saw something glinting in a garden.
A jug!
A big clay jug, under a tree.
The crow quickly flew down.
He looked into the jug.
Yes, there was water in it!
But oh dear.
The water was right at the bottom.
And the jug had a long, narrow neck.
The crow put his beak in.
He couldn't reach.
He stretched his neck as far as he could.
Still not.
He tried to push the jug over.
Push!
Push!
But the jug was too heavy.
What now?
The crow sat on the edge and thought.
He thought and thought.
He looked around.
On the ground there were lots of little pebbles.
Round pebbles, flat pebbles, white and grey pebbles.
And then he had an idea!
He picked up a pebble in his beak and dropped it into the jug.
Plop!
He took another pebble.
Plop!
And another one.
Plop!
And do you know what happened?
Every time a pebble fell into the jug, the water came up a tiny bit higher.
The pebbles pushed the water up!
The crow worked very hard.
One, two, three, ten, twenty pebbles.
Plop, plop, plop.
The water came higher, and higher, and even higher.
Until it was almost at the top.
Then the crow put his beak into the jug, and he drank.
Slurp, slurp, slurp!
The water was fresh and cool.
Mmm!
How lovely!
The crow drank until he wasn't thirsty anymore.
Then he sat in the shade of the tree and sang a happy song.
Caw, caw, cawww!
A little sparrow had seen everything.
How clever you are, crow!
said the sparrow.
The crow laughed.
I'm not stronger than anyone else, he said.
But if you don't give up, and you think hard, you'll always find a way.
And he let the sparrow drink too.
